column3: Close to the Hebrew; NKJV capitalizes “the Spirit of God.”
Close to the Hebrew; “whose eyes are opened” renders an uncertain word that may also mean “whose eye is closed” (also in verse 15).
Close to the Hebrew; “the Almighty” renders “Shaddai” (also in verse 16).
Close to the Hebrew; “valleys” renders “wadis,” and “aloes” is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; the Greek reads differently here (“a man shall come forth from his seed … higher than Gog”).
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV capitalizes “Him,” “Star,” and “Scepter,” a messianic reading; the Hebrew has “him,” “a star,” and “a scepter.” “sons of tumult” renders “sons of Sheth.”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV capitalizes “One”; the Hebrew has only “he shall have dominion.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Kain” is the name of the Kenites' ancestor.
